title: Allocations can fail while reclaimable empty blocks remain cached
body:
On main fc22df0, each backend retains an empty general block. A new allocation in another memory type can fail while those empty blocks still hold native memory; the failure path does not reclaim them and retry. Growable preferred blocks can also exceed available memory even when a smaller block sufficient for the resource would succeed.

Deterministic reproducer: keep one occupied GPU-only block and one emptied CPU-accessible cached block; impose a native allocation limit that permits the requested resource after the cache is released but rejects the preferred new block while the cache remains. The reviewed driver-stub reproducer fails without recovery and succeeds after releasing empty blocks. A separate 48 MiB/two-block control serves 48 one-MiB requests with 32+16 MiB shared blocks, versus two requests with a single exact-size fallback policy. These are synthetic limits, not hardware-budget claims.

The proposed #323 update reuses compatible Vulkan blocks first, reclaims empty caches only on recoverable pressure, retries when reclamation changed state, and reduces preferred Vulkan/D3D12 block sizes toward the aligned resource floor. Fatal and allocation-count errors do not trigger size retries. Metal's untyped nil uses a conservative exact-floor attempt and commits pending residency removals; Apple runtime validation remains outstanding. Per-type bounded caches and indexed trim/cached_capacity/trim_to APIs make retention explicit. Physical heap capacity is not an OS budget.

Related: #96 (manual cache reclamation), #125 (allocation count), #322 (sizing threshold), and the independent Vulkan contracts fix https://github.com/Traverse-Research/gpu-allocator/pull/328. This report concerns allocation reliability, without claiming a particular public trimming interface is mandatory.

Agent-assisted investigation and report. Evidence: https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/allocator-reconciliation-20261128
